dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "17 West-region annual-plan renewals were posted on 31 May, totaling $1,506.29."
"The two May dealer batches reconcile exactly to the recharge data: $723.42 + $782.87 = $1,506.29 with no cash-to-ledger difference."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The 17 renewals have effective event dates between 1–28 May, while posted_at is concentrated on 31 May."
"The same month-end batch behavior appears in other months, indicating a recurring submission/posting process rather than an isolated ingestion failure."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "The reconciliation email is therefore treated as context, not proof; the conclusion relies primarily on the transaction-level and import-log checks."
"The supplied evidence does not independently establish every underlying customer-payment or entitlement fact."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "The decision would change if additional evidence showed: the same customer was economically renewed more than once; bank/payment records failed to support the dealer cash totals; ... or entitlement, cancellation, or reversal records contradicted the 17 renewals."

"For the weekly retention trend pack, use effective_event_date rather than posted_at when measuring renewal activity. This is reversible, avoids distorting the operational trend, and does not alter booked revenue."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Final escalation judgment: NO MATERIAL ISSUE — the evidence supports an expected contractual month-end batch, not duplicate revenue, manipulation, or a pipeline defect."
"Do not reverse or suppress the 31 May revenue."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "No material issue" and "expected contractual month-end batch" are somewhat stronger than the evidence supports because the contractual explanation is based on the reconciliation email and the submission does not independently verify its applicability to these specific dealer batches.

"with no cash-to-ledger difference" demonstrates reconciliation to the recorded recharge/import totals, but does not establish independent bank or payment settlement support; the submission itself acknowledges that bank/payment evidence is unknown.

"No duplicate source_event_id or recharge_id was identified" does not by itself test duplicate economic entitlement, customer payment, cancellation, reversal, or overlapping coverage. The submission identifies these as unknowns but does not perform the entitlement check expected by the exercise.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled the principal alternatives—duplicate revenue, manipulated reporting, and a pipeline defect—by citing unique identifiers, import acceptance, reconciliation, and the separation of effective_event_date from posted_at. The main alternative it missed as a completed test was an economically duplicated entitlement or unsupported customer cash position despite technically unique source events.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Perform and cite an explicit entitlement and independent cash-support reconciliation for the two dealer cohorts—joining renewals to coverage, cancellation/reversal, and customer/payment records, with dealer IDs and row-level results—before treating the conclusion as definitive.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Observed fact: South tickets fell from 318 in Mar 19-May 9 to 196 in May 10-Jun 30. | tickets.csv | High"
"Observed fact: IVR case creation fell from 106/197 sessions, 53.8%, to 94/2709, 3.5%. | ivr_interactions.jsonl, tickets.csv | High"

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The case decline is more consistent with measurement leakage or case suppression than proven complaint reduction"
"Farah says containment starts only after subscriber identification, while pre-auth exits are excluded from CareDesk case reporting."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Material unknowns: customer satisfaction after IVR exits, repeat contact across non-IVR channels, whether abandoned/error sessions later became complaints"
"NovaIVR may resolve some simple balance or pack-info needs, but that benefit is mixed with high errors and abandons."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do not expand nationally yet."
"Hold national rollout. Fix authentication and prompt-timing issues, then run a two-week controlled test using matched non-pilot regions and full-funnel metrics"

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Question Farah Iqbal, Director, Customer Care Operations."
"Which NovaIVR terminal stages are counted as contained on the dashboard, and which stages are excluded from CareDesk reporting?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The judgment states that "errors, abandons, and repeat contacts rose," but the evidence table does not provide evidence that repeat contacts rose; later, repeat contacts are correctly listed as an unknown.

"South service-impact events increased after the pilot" is an observed count comparison, but it does not by itself reject improved service quality because exposure, affected-account rates, and event severity are not normalized.
The statement that "many failures appear" in pre-authentication stages is stronger than the cited exclusion rule alone supports unless the session-level stage distribution is explicitly shown.
"Fix authentication and prompt-timing issues" presumes those are established causes; the submission identifies them as questions and possible failure points rather than demonstrating causality.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst partially handles the benign alternative that NovaIVR resolved some simple balance or pack-information needs and notes that channel shifting may have occurred. However, it does not fully test whether the increased IVR volume reflects successful substitution or whether raw error and abandonment counts simply rose because sessions increased substantially; rates and linked customer outcomes are needed.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Remove the unsupported claim that repeat contacts rose and produce a session-linked funnel with normalized rates and downstream outcomes—repeat contacts, transfers, cases, resolution, and sampled call results—before attributing the case decline to either improvement or suppression.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission directly cites `inverter_events.csv`, including its 4 data rows, date range, `cleared=yes`, `impact_mw=0`, severity counts, and 1–7 minute durations.
The claim is appropriately scoped in the evidence table as “No event-row evidence of operational escalation.”

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: It tests a plausible innocent explanation—“Export may be narrow or filtered”—and proposes checking “filters/time window/source export settings.”
It correctly avoids treating event wording alone as proof of equipment failure, stating: “Event wording alone is not enough to infer equipment failure.”
The reasoning is primarily based on one event-export channel and does not independently cross-check communications, plant telemetry, or another operational log.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The export-scope concern is labeled “Confidence: Medium,” while the row-level observations are labeled “Confidence: High.”
The conclusion preserves uncertainty by saying to escalate only “if records are missing.”
The “Rejected” conclusion has somewhat excessive confidence because a narrow or incomplete export cannot by itself reject every possibility of an active inverter problem.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation—“Perform one cheap check: confirm the export filters/time window and row count”—is low-cost, proportionate, and directly discriminates between a genuinely small dataset and a data-quality problem.
It appropriately says to stop if the small scope is intentional rather than searching for a plant-failure narrative.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion matches the supplied event evidence: all rows are cleared, have zero MW impact, and are short-duration informational or warning events.
It identifies the export scope as the only worthwhile follow-up and does not invent a plant problem from the warning-level event.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “The evidence rejects” an “active or high-impact inverter failure” is too broad: the cited rows strongly argue against a high-impact event in this export, but a potentially incomplete export cannot fully reject an active issue outside its scope.
“Only smell worth checking” is a prioritization judgment rather than a directly demonstrated fact, although it is reasonable given the cited zero-impact, cleared events.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The four rows may be a deliberately limited export or a communications/monitoring warning rather than a plant event. If the filter and time window are confirmed, the evidence supports stopping without further operational escalation; if not, the principal issue is export completeness rather than inverter failure.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Make the rejection explicitly scope-limited: state that the export provides no evidence of a high-impact or unresolved event, while reserving judgment about events omitted by the export; then verify the export filters/time window against the intended analysis scope.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: “From dispatch_blocks.csv, 2026-05-28 sums to Rs 662444.09 DSM penalty and 2026-05-29 sums to Rs 453085.88” provides specific source and figures.
“The impact note makes a stronger impact-style claim than the data can causally prove” correctly links the causal limitation to AI_Pilot_Impact_Note.md.
The submission does not cite the specific base_schedule_mw and submitted_schedule_mw fields needed for the same-day counterfactual.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: It correctly notes that “weather severity, forecast error, day selection, availability, curtailment, operator behavior, and revision timing could explain some or all of the difference.”

It tests arithmetic error and recognizes the comparison is across different days, but does not construct or discuss the required same-day comparison of base_schedule_mw versus submitted_schedule_mw on 2026-05-29.
“Rejected hypothesis 2: The result is worthless evidence” is a weakly framed alternative and does not genuinely resolve the key causal alternatives.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: “The 31.6% penalty reduction is reproducible as an observed two-day comparison, not as a proven causal pilot impact” is appropriately scoped.
“What remains unidentified is causality” clearly identifies material unknowns.
The calibration is incomplete because it omits the smaller same-day benefit, which would support a more precise conclusion than simply comparing two different days.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: “Continue the pilot only as controlled high-wind support with operator review” is proportionate and preserves operational safeguards.
The proposed “matched high-wind validation” is a sensible next test and uses common actual generation and settlement logic.
The proposed validation is less targeted than it could be because it does not explicitly require reporting the 2026-05-29 base-versus-submitted same-day counterfactual first.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion correctly distinguishes a reproducible two-day observation from a causal 31.6% impact.

It misses the central same-day result: comparing base_schedule_mw with submitted_schedule_mw on 2026-05-29 indicates a smaller benefit, so the evidence supports some pilot value while undermining the headline causal interpretation.

“The narrower defensible claim is that the AI-assisted comparison day had lower summed DSM penalty” remains focused on the cross-day comparison and is under-scoped relative to the available same-day evidence.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “The data rejects [the hypothesis that] the result is worthless evidence” overstates what the comparison establishes; it shows potentially useful directional evidence, not a validated pilot effect.

The claim that the comparison day had lower absolute block-level schedule gap is traceable as a cross-day aggregate, but it is not a substitute for the same-day base_schedule_mw versus submitted_schedule_mw counterfactual.
The submission implies that matched validation is the first necessary basis for assessing value, while the supplied 2026-05-29 fields already permit a smaller same-day benefit estimate.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 2026-05-29 same-day counterfactual suggests the pilot produced a smaller but real improvement when submitted_schedule_mw is compared with base_schedule_mw using the same day's generation and settlement logic. Thus the pilot may have operational value, but the 31.6% figure is a favorable cross-day comparison rather than a controlled causal estimate.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Recalculate and report the 2026-05-29 same-day counterfactual explicitly: compare DSM penalty and schedule-gap outcomes under base_schedule_mw versus submitted_schedule_mw, then present that smaller effect separately from the 31.6% cross-day figure.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Packet CH-2025-000522 declared P1001 Titanium acetabular cup as 90211000 in Switzerland."
"Swiss working classification for P1001 is 90211000, effective 2025-01-01 with no end date shown."
"The canonical schema lacks code-system, nomenclature version, effective dates, ruling authority, and superseded-submission fields"

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "Rejected: 'The declaration is likely wrong because Helios says 90211090.'"
"Rejected: 'This is an origin or preference issue.'"
"Rejected: 'The Swiss code is stale.'"

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "probable code-system/comparator false positive"
"this remains only a working classification"
"could materially change the judgment"

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "an 8-digit string comparison can confuse Swiss local tariff codes with Helios/CN-style codes."
"Country matrix warns Switzerland uses a Swiss local tariff code and matching strings across jurisdictions is not expected."
"Helios master lists P1001 as 90211090, but the product master is current commercial master data, not customs-ruling status."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Close this as not a likely declaration error for now, log a comparator false-positive reason, and ask the Swiss trade owner or broker to confirm 90211000 against Tares/ruling evidence for P1001 on 2025-11-04 before any corrective filing."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The conclusion that this is a "probable" comparator false positive is reasonable but not fully confirmed because the submission lacks official Swiss Tares/ruling evidence and Helios mapping provenance.
"Close this as not a likely declaration error" is appropriately qualified by "for now," but the submission does not specify whether the case should remain open pending the requested confirmation.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: 90211090 could still be the applicable Swiss classification, or the Swiss matrix could be an internal working classification rather than the legally controlling code; official Tares or product-specific ruling evidence and Helios mapping provenance are needed to exclude that possibility.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain and cite the official Swiss Tares/ruling result and the effective-date provenance for the Helios-to-Swiss mapping before closing the case.

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing

"Rejected: ‘United States manufacturing origin disproves preference by itself.’ Manufacturing country is not the same as preferential origin."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "Workshop notes warn that ERP/manufacturing origin is not designed to prove preference and that Irish checks need the supplier declaration and rule used for the claim."
"supplier declarations may sit in category folders and the register is not always updated when sourcing routes change."
"Automated note says a preference indicator is present but supplier support is not linked in ClearView."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Safe action now is to hold the preference support as unverified, retrieve the supplier declaration/rule basis from Procurement or broker files, and only maintain the claim if current, product-specific support is produced."
"Do not clear the preference claim as supported from this packet."
"if not produced promptly, flag the entry for customs review and consider correction or duty exposure assessment."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The submission states that the expired register row "cannot support this claim without renewal or separate evidence." This is substantively reasonable, but it would be stronger if it explicitly distinguished an expired register entry from the underlying declaration's legal validity and assessed whether the applicable origin rule permits other evidence for the shipment period.

The phrase "only SUP-02/P1006 reference expired" depends on the completeness of the supplied register/search results; the submission appropriately limits this by noting that documents may exist outside the register.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: A current, product-specific supplier declaration and applicable preferential-origin rule may exist in Procurement, a category folder, broker workpapers, or an unlinked ClearView record. If that evidence covers 2025-09-18 and supports the qualifying rule, the preference could be valid; the current packet demonstrates an evidence gap rather than fraud or invalidity.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain and quote the actual current SUP-02/P1006 supplier declaration and its preferential-origin rule basis, then test that rule against the product and shipment date rather than relying primarily on the register's expiration status.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "SOP target is routine material release within 24 hours from required evidence available to disposition"; "185 of 220 completed records have `qcore_release_ts` exactly at `02:10:00`"; sources identified as `qc_release_sop.md`, QCore, LabTrack, and CertVault.
"Include at least a few held Riverbend rows where evidence appears available but no release timestamp exists."],

Citations are specific to the SOP, fields, timestamp value, record count, and proposed comparison records, with useful cross-system triangulation. It does not explicitly address whether the extracts are a coherent point-in-time snapshot.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "The bigger smell is that 185 of 220 completed records have `qcore_release_ts` exactly at `02:10:00`, matching the QCore daily interface snapshot pattern rather than looking like actual disposition event times."
"reconcile it to the native QCore disposition audit timestamp, LabTrack completion timestamp, and CertVault CoA availability timestamp."],

The submission distinguishes the observed KPI from a possible interface-timing mechanism and proposes a discriminating reconciliation. However, its lab-complete comparison does not fully establish the SOP-defined required-evidence event.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "I would verify the cycle-time definition and timestamp lineage before using 'about a day and a half' as a QC release KPI."
"The extract can produce a median receipt-to-release time of about 39.4 hours" and "the median lab-complete-to-release time is about 17.9 hours."
"Smallest verification: for 10-15 batches, ask Quality/Data Catalog to confirm what `qcore_release_ts` represents."],
The analyst appropriately treats the KPI and timestamp meaning as provisional and proposes a bounded sample. It does not explicitly quantify or discuss the source-freshness mismatch between extracts.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "I would verify the cycle-time definition and timestamp lineage before using 'about a day and a half' as a QC release KPI."
"Smallest verification: for 10-15 batches" with reconciliation to native audit, LabTrack, and CertVault timestamps.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "matching the QCore daily interface snapshot pattern rather than looking like actual disposition event times"
"Include at least a few held Riverbend rows where evidence appears available but no release timestamp exists."],

It advances an interface-snapshot explanation and tests it against native audit data and held records. It does not clearly state the strongest alternative explanation or what evidence would revive it beyond the proposed reconciliation.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "for 10-15 batches, ask Quality/Data Catalog to confirm what `qcore_release_ts` represents and reconcile it to the native QCore disposition audit timestamp, LabTrack completion timestamp, and CertVault CoA availability timestamp."
"Include at least a few held Riverbend rows where evidence appears available but no release timestamp exists."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: Calling the lab-complete-to-release metric an "SOP-aligned" routine measure is not fully supported: the SOP start point is when all required evidence is available to disposition, which may differ from lab completion.

The statement that the 02:10 timestamps match a daily interface snapshot pattern is a strong hypothesis, but it remains unconfirmed until native QCore audit timestamps and interface lineage are reconciled.
The submission does not explicitly establish that QCore, LabTrack, and CertVault extracts represent the same point-in-time snapshot.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 02:10:00 concentration could reflect a genuine operational practice in which dispositions are consistently performed at that time, or a legitimate but delayed batch interface that preserves a valid release event while shifting its recorded timestamp. Native QCore audit events and interface commit metadata would distinguish these explanations.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Replace the lab-complete-to-release comparison with a reconstructed SOP event timestamp for "required evidence available to disposition," using aligned source snapshots or event-level timestamps, and then compare that metric with the QCore interface timestamp.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: “Live local CMMS stock and reservation status”
“engineering equivalence signoff for semantic-only matches”
“confirmation that available quantities are not double-counted across simultaneous requests”
“receiving-site qualification detail for site-specific parts, and current ProcureNet request status”

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The “actionable now” amount is somewhat overstated or insufficiently bounded because the submission itself says the global MaintStar snapshot is stale and requests live local confirmation before relying on availability and reservation status.

The exact bucket totals are presented with only medium confidence and without row-level allocation or explicit proof that stock is not concurrently committed across all requests, although the analyst identifies this missing test.
“Common qualification” and transferability for some exact-MPN candidates are asserted in the candidate table but are not shown with specific restriction fields or row references.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The semantic-search opportunity may be materially smaller than the 17.2% actionable estimate because the enterprise extracts are temporally inconsistent: live local reservations, qualification, duplicate allocations, and current request status could invalidate some apparent exact-MPN matches. Conversely, the opportunity could increase if currently reserved or stale records are released, so the present buckets are screening estimates rather than realized savings.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run a live, point-in-time allocation check for the highest-value candidate matches—especially the exact-MPN pump, servo/drive, valve, and filter candidates—joining unrestricted quantity, revision/UOM, qualification, reservation, and concurrent-request allocation. Recalculate the three buckets from that coherent snapshot and define pilot success as precision of engineering-approved, actually transferable candidates rather than semantic-hit count.
